title: 1. What is a soul made of?
md:
**The question.** What kind of stuff is a soul? The answers on Source Library's pages run from breath, fire,
blood and atoms, through ratios and numbers, to a substance with no size, and to the claim that there is no such
stuff. This page sorts them by kind of stuff, not by century.

**How to read it.** Claims are ✓ verified unless marked ◐ (hedged) or ○ (Open questions only). Quotes are SL's
English, a model translation, unless the book is English or the original is given. Tag: `q:made-of`.

**The short answer.**
- **Breath or wind**: Stoics, Tertullian, Epicurus; Tylor's breath-word history of psychē, nefesh, anima
  [[5]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-stoics-soul-connate-pneuma-survives-until-conflagration) [[6]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-tertullian-soul-shape-of-its-body) [[7]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-tylor-breath-words-table).
- **Fire, heat, aether**: Democritus, the Pythagorean notes, the Hermetic "fiery tunic"
  [[8]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-democritus-spherical-atoms-fire-soul) [[9]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoreans-soul-distinct-from-life) [[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-hermetica-ch10-fiery-tunic).
- **Blood or water**: Critias and Hippo, as Aristotle reports them [[11]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-critias-soul-is-blood).
- **Atoms**: Democritus and Epicurus; Plotinus against them [[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-epicurus-soul-fine-particles-wind-heat) [[13]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-plotinus-iv7-not-atoms).
- **A harmony, ratio or blend**: rejected by Nemesius and, in effect, by Avicenna [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-nemesius-temperament-is-not-the-soul) [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#isl-crit-flying-man-temperament).
- **Number**: a self-moving number (Xenocrates), a soul divided by number (Philolaus via Mamertus, Psellos)
  [[16]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plutarch-xenocrates-ousia-number-moved-by-itself) [[17]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-psellos-soul-sevenfold).
- **The form of the body**: Aristotle, Aquinas, the Council of Vienne [[18]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-aquinas-soul-not-body-but-act-of-body) [[19]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-vienne-anima-forma-corporis).
- **An immaterial substance**: Plato, Augustine, Nemesius, Avicenna, Proclus, the Nyāya and the Jains
  [[20]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-nemesius-soul-incorporeal-substance) [[21]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-186-self-reversion-incorporeal) [[22]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-jain-niyamasara-only-conscious-substance).
- **Qi**: in the Chinese texts hun and po are qi, gathered and dispersed [[23]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zhuxi-guishen-only-qi).
- **Nothing**: no self among the aggregates (the Buddha), a name with no object (Kant), a vain term (La Mettrie)
  [[24]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-vinaya-anattalakkhana) [[25]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-kant-soul-name-for-transcendental-object) [[26]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-lamettrie-soul-vain-term).

---

## A. Breath and wind

The Stoics make the soul the breath born with us, and so a body:

> "And they regard it as the breath of life, congenital with us; from which they infer first that it is a body and
> secondly that it survives death. Yet it is perishable" [[5]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-stoics-soul-connate-pneuma-survives-until-conflagration)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhAwalpTYhD8XcOymwb (πνεῦμα συμφυές)

Tertullian takes this over for Christianity. The soul "in its material nature¹ it is wind and breath, (or spirit)"
(*flatus*, *spiritus*) [[6]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-tertullian-soul-shape-of-its-body) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhApeqgUU5RkZDU8VZL.
He enlists Zeno's syllogism [[27]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-tertullian-enlists-zeno-cleanthes) and gives the soul length, breadth, height
and a figure [[28]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-tertullian-soul-has-figure-and-dimensions).

For Democritus, breathing keeps the soul-atoms in [[29]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-democritus-breathing-keeps-soul-atoms-in).

Tylor (1871) made it a rule: nephesh, ruach, nefs, ātman, psychē and anima all start as "breath": "The same is the history of Sanskrit âtman and prâna, of Greek psychē and pneuma, of Latin animus, anima,
spiritus" [[7]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-tylor-breath-words-table) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOfQQIcrpOnWm73Cpr. The critique below
says why that etymology does not give one concept [[30]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-etymology-is-not-meaning).

## B. Fire, heat and aether

Aristotle reports: "This is what led Democritus to say that soul is a sort of fire or hot substance". The spherical
atoms were chosen because that shape moves best through everything [[8]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-democritus-spherical-atoms-fire-soul)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bkp1LfgqJZJGMHrwQhP. The Pythagorean notes in Diogenes Laertius use heat for *life* and
aether for *soul*:

> "All things live which partake of heat—this is why plants are living things—but all do not have a soul. The soul
> is a detached part of aether" [[9]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoreans-soul-distinct-from-life) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhAwalpTYhD8XcOymxx
> (ἀπόσπασμα αἰθέρος)

In the Hermetic *Key*, minds freed from the earthly body "immediately put on their own tunic, the fiery one" (χιτὼν πύρινος), which earth could not bear [[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-hermetica-ch10-fiery-tunic) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BejFoukEepZzy8QxT0F.
Plotinus notes that the Stoics themselves move toward a better view when they make the soul an intellectual spirit
and fire (πῦρ νοερόν) [[31]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-plotinus-iv7-against-stoic-pneuma).

## C. Blood and water

Aristotle again: Hippo made the soul water, from the fluid seed. "Another group (Critias, for example) did hold it to
be blood; they take perception to be the most characteristic attribute of soul" [[11]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-critias-soul-is-blood)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bkp1LfgqJZJGMHrwQhT (αἷμα). Saint-Martin's *âme de sang* is a late echo [[32]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-render-ame-charnelle-saint-martin).
Avicenna's floating man denies it from the inside: he affirms his self but "nor heart, nor blood" (ولا قلبا ولا دما)
[[33]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-flying-man-not-heart-blood) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhibVye1RH7VxgfG0pL. Where the blood sits
in the body is on page 02.

## D. Atoms and fine particles

Epicurus gives the fullest atomist answer:

> "the soul is a physical thing, composed of fine particles, dispersed all over the frame" [[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-epicurus-soul-fine-particles-wind-heat)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhAwalpTYhD8XcOyn1x (ψυχὴ σῶμα λεπτομερές)

Because it is a body it scatters at death, and only the void is incorporeal
[[34]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-epicurus-soul-scattered-incorporeal-foolish). Plotinus answers that only soul can supply the
forming reason that makes a body: "For reason cannot proceed from any thing else than from soul"
[[13]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-plotinus-iv7-not-atoms) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bi8TYwtni7t7sPx5onn. Aristotle's sharpest objection to
the number-soul (section F) is that it turns out to be atomism in disguise.

## E. A harmony, a ratio, a blend

The harmony-soul belongs to harmony-kb (Simmias in the *Phaedo*: [[1]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-phaedo-soul-not-attunement);
Aristotle's rejection: [[2]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-aristotle-soul-not-harmony)). Here it appears in its medical form, the soul as
the body's *krasis* (blend). Nemesius refutes it: a blend changes with diet and season, and

> "the temperament does not oppose the desires of the body, but rather cooperates with them … The soul, however, does
> oppose these desires. Therefore, the temperament is not the soul." [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-nemesius-temperament-is-not-the-soul)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUueghyIdnCELWcZPL (οὐκ ἄρα ἡ κρᾶσίς ἐστι ψυχή)

Avicenna raises the same option against his own floating man. What is self-perceived might be the temperament
(*mizāj*). He answers only that "the temperament is only perceived through affection" [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#isl-crit-flying-man-temperament)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhibVye1RH7VxgfG0pL. (On Heraclitus' logos rendered "proportion", see [[35]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-heraclitus-soul-limits-deep-logos-rendered-proportion).)

## F. Number: the self-moving number and its line (thread:number)

The question here is whether a soul is a mathematical
structure, and if so, what kind.

**The definition.** The oldest witness gives it to no one by name:

> "Some thinkers, accepting both premisses, viz. that the soul is both originative of movement and cognitive, have
> compounded it of both and declared the soul to be a self-moving number." [[36]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-xenocrates-self-moving-number-compound)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bkp1LfgqJZJGMHrwQhR (ἀριθμὸν κινοῦνθ' ἑαυτόν)

So the formula joins the two marks the earlier thinkers had fixed on, movement and knowing
[[37]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-predecessors-movement-and-sensation). Plutarch names the author and ties the formula to the soul's
mixture in *Timaeus* 35: "Xenocrates, who declared the ousia of the soul to be a number moved by itself" (τῆς ψυχῆς
τὴν οὐσίαν ἀριθμὸν αὐτὸν ὑφ’ ἑαυτοῦ κινούμενον) [[16]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plutarch-xenocrates-ousia-number-moved-by-itself)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhIg7dUhprQUmpSBjGA. Aëtius puts it under Pythagoras, "a number moving itself, taking
"number" to stand for "intellect."" (τὸν δ' ἀριθμὸν ἀντὶ τοῦ νοῦ) [[38]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-aetius-pythagoras-number-moving-itself).
He gives Plato "an intelligible substance, moving of itself, in accordance with harmonic number"
[[39]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-aetius-plato-soul-harmonic-number) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhD0tyWfEXb66hzf2ON. Aristotle also reports the
Academy's lectures, in which the soul's powers *are* numbers: "Mind is the monad, science or knowledge the dyad …
opinion the number of the plane,⁴ sensation the number of the solid" [[40]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plato-lectures-mind-monad-dyad).

**Aristotle's verdict.** "by far the most unreasonable is that which declares the soul to be a self-moving number"
[[41]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-self-moving-number-most-unreasonable) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bkp1LfgqJZJGMHrwQhc. Moving units
trace lines, "for a point is a unit having position, and the number of the soul is, of course, somewhere and has
position". A number minus a unit is a different number, yet a cut plant lives on. Units with position are just
Democritus' round atoms shrunk to points [[42]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-grk-number-soul-collapses-into-atoms).

**Philolaus via Mamertus.** Claudianus Mamertus (c. 469) quotes a book of Philolaus, *On Rhythms and Measures*:

> "The soul is placed into the body … through number and an immortal and incorporeal harmony." [[43]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-mamertus-philolaus-number-harmony)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUuUqHu9PeRkqljwVy (anima inditur corpori per numerum et inmortalem eandemque incorporalem conuenientiam)

Mamertus does not make the soul a number. Number is the soul's way *into* the body. Bodies carry traces of numbers
(*uestigia numerorum*): "every body can be divided into parts, of which any part of the body—because of the
primordial power of number—will also be one body" [[44]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-mamertus-traces-of-number-in-bodies)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUuUqHu9PeRkqljwVo. The soul's own greatness is "by virtue, not by mass" (*uirtute, non
mole*) [[45]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-mamertus-soul-greater-by-virtue-not-mass). So in Mamertus number marks the body, and the soul has
quality without quantity.

**Psellos' sevenfold number.** Expounding *Timaeus* 35 (the ratios are in [[3]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-timaeus-world-soul-ratios)),
Psellos (c. 1050) writes:

> "For it has been divided in this way according to an essential number into seven terms: 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 8, 27."
> [[17]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-psellos-soul-sevenfold) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUvuTdN6E14yky9Fnv (κατ' ἀριθμὸν οὐσιώδη εἰς ὅρους ἑπτά)

The soul is therefore sevenfold, proportional and cyclic; the returning numbers 3, 9, 27 are like circles. Proclus
has the world soul split the whole in two "according to the essential dyad" (κατὰ τὴν δυάδα τὴν οὐσιώδη)
[[46]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-timaeus-soul-divides-by-dyad). He also makes the ranks of souls and of their vehicles a single
proportion [[47]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-205-vehicle-proportion). In this line number is the soul's *essence* (οὐσιώδης), not its
measure.

**Where it leaves the machine question.** On the KB's machine table the definition cuts at the start of the motion:
a computer is number moved by something else [[48]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-row-xenocrates-self-moving-number). That is page 08's question.

## G. The form of the body

Aristotle's soul as first entelechy of a natural organic body belongs to aliveness-kb
([[4]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-deanima-soul-first-entelechy-organic-body)). Aquinas gives the scholastic form of it:

> "The soul, therefore, which is the first principle of life, is not a body but the act of a body"
> [[18]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-aquinas-soul-not-body-but-act-of-body) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPwp560jwjz5r3SiGP (*actus corporis*)

The intellect itself "is the form of the human body" [[49]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-aquinas-intellect-is-form-of-body),
and it is the only substantial form in man [[50]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-aquinas-one-substantial-form). In 1312 the Council of Vienne made the denial heretical [[19]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-vienne-anima-forma-corporis)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BlPNxzPqv51yHbhWXPj. Spinoza keeps the pairing without the hierarchy: the object of the
mind is "the Body, or a certain mode of Extension actually existing, and nothing else" [[51]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-spinoza-mind-idea-of-body).

Fan Zhen's *Shenmie lun* (c. 500) gives a Chinese form-and-function answer. Spirit is to the body as sharpness to a
blade (神之於質猶利之於刃), and no one has heard of the blade gone and the sharpness remaining (our paraphrase of
未聞刃没而利存) [[52]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-fanzhen-blade-sharpness) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl0ad19SZvZr6DQymMF.

## H. An immaterial substance

The largest family. The arguments differ more than the conclusion.

- **From affinity.** The *Phaedo*: "the divine is by nature fitted to rule and lead, and the mortal to obey and
  serve", so the soul is most like the divine [[53]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plato-phaedo-affinity).
- **From having no size.** Augustine: the soul "is not long, nor wide, nor robust, nor any of those things which are
  wont to be sought in the measures of bodies" [[54]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-augustine-quantity-of-soul-not-long-or-wide)
  https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPvDqYfJ7JXfgk7m8l. Al-Kindī: "the soul is not a body nor is it circumscribed"
  [[55]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-kindi-soul-not-body-not-circumscribed). Descartes: "a half or a third part of the soul can in no way be
  conceived" [[56]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-no-half-soul). Al-Ghazālī's spirit "which we call heart" has no size or divisibility
  [[57]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-heart-spirit-no-quantity).
- **From self-knowledge.** Augustine: the mind is certain it lives and understands but not "whether it is air or
  fire … Therefore, it is in no way some body" [[58]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-augustine-mind-certain-of-itself-not-body). Proclus: what knows
  itself turns back on itself, and "every body is devoid of the power to turn toward itself"
  [[21]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-186-self-reversion-incorporeal) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUvVF7tfKHgyDbC4Np. Avicenna's floating man and Ibn Ṭufayl argue the same way
  [[33]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-flying-man-not-heart-blood) [[59]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ibntufayl-knowing-essence-noncorporeal).
- **From elimination.** Nemesius: "If we have demonstrated that the soul is neither a body, nor a harmony , nor a
  mixture , nor any other quality, it is clear from this that the soul is an incorporeal substance"
  [[20]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-nemesius-soul-incorporeal-substance) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUueghyIdnCELWcZPu (οὐσία τις ἐστὶν ἀσώματος).
  Avicenna's rational soul is "not a body, nor has it being on account of the body" [[60]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-rational-soul-not-imprinted). So the Ikhwān [[61]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ikhwan-soul-substance-not-accident).
- **From marks.** The Nyāya gives desire, aversion, effort, pleasure, pain and cognition as the ātman's marks
  [[62]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-nyaya-marks-of-atman). The Jain *Niyamasāra*: "The soul. It is the only conscious substance."
  [[22]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-jain-niyamasara-only-conscious-substance); the jīva is formless and the size of its body [[63]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-jain-jiva-definition).
  Wolff argues from simplicity [[64]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-wolff-731-simple-substance-cannot-perish).

**A thinner body.** Several traditions refuse the choice between body and no body. Faustus of Riez gives the soul "a
body by which they subsist, though much and incomparably thinner than our bodies", so that nothing is incorporeal but
God (*nihil esse incorporeum, nisi solum deum*) [[65]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-faustus-nothing-incorporeal-but-god)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUuUqHu9PeRkqljwUC. Henry More's soul is "a Substance extended and indiscerpible"
[[66]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-more-soul-extended-indiscerpible), with an "Essential Spissitude" in place of a fourth dimension
[[67]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-more-essential-spissitude). The Neoplatonists give the soul a vehicle (ὄχημα), "the first body of the soul"
[[68]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-synesius-pneuma-first-body), "immaterial, indivisible in essence, and impassive"
[[69]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-vehicle-impassive-same-shape), which descends by putting on more material tunics
[[70]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-209-vehicle-tunics); the Oracles knew only one vehicle [[71]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-kroll-oracles-one-vehicle). Kardec's
*périsprit* [[72]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-kardec-perispirit-semi-material-envelope) and Leadbeater's astral body [[73]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-leadbeater-three-corpses)
are its modern heirs. Budge's English puts the Egyptian ka and ba in the same class [[74]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1913-ka-renderings-birch)
[[75]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1913-ba-heart-soul). Jain karma, by contrast, is the matter that clogs the jīva [[76]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-jain-karma-is-matter).

## I. Qi

In the Chinese sources the question has no separate soul-stuff to work with. The Huainanzi says "天氣為 魂地氣為魄"
(the qi of heaven is hun, the qi of earth is po) [[77]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-huainanzi-heaven-qi-hun-earth-qi-po)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl11R9VvglG7RgSEdCv. Zheng Xuan glosses breathing as qi and the acuity of ear and eye as po [[78]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-liji-jiyi-qi-shen-po-gui). The Liji has "魂氣歸於天形魄歸於地": the hun-qi returns to heaven and
the form-po to earth [[79]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-liji-hunqi-heaven-xingpo-earth). Zhu Xi is the shortest:

> "鬼神只是氣屈伸往来者氣也天地間無非氣" (our paraphrase: gui and shen are only qi, what bends and stretches, goes and
> comes; between heaven and earth there is nothing that is not qi) [[23]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zhuxi-guishen-only-qi) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl0Z7VrdSkq9cVOvXbZ

Zhang Zai and the *Xingli daquan* say the same [[80]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zhangzai-guishen-liangneng) [[81]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-guishen-expansion-contraction-of-qi).
Qi is breath, but it is also everything, so this is not "breath" in the Stoic sense (page 04).

## J. Nothing

- **No self among the parts.** "The body (Rûpa), O Bhikkhus, is not the self." The same is said of each of the five
  aggregates [[24]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-vinaya-anattalakkhana) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhPXIeb5uGyl6M9xHQ8. Nāgasena: "Chariot is a
  mere empty sound" [[82]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-milinda-chariot-designation). The *Kathāvatthu* refutes the person as found in the
  sense of ultimate reality (*saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena*) [[83]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-kathavatthu-puggala-ultimate-reality).
- **No describable stuff.** The Upaniṣadic ātman is not nothing. It is "not this, it is not that (neti, neti)"
  [[84]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-brihad-neti-neti), the inner controller of earth, wind and breath [[85]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-brihad-antaryamin-inner-controller).
- **A name with no object.** Kant: the soul is a name for the transcendental object, and "This expression
  nevertheless has no application that extends to actual objects" [[25]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-kant-soul-name-for-transcendental-object)
  [[86]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-kant-paralogism-sophisma-figurae-dictionis). Brentano reports Lange's "Psychologie ohne Seele"
  [[87]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-brentano-lange-psychology-without-soul); James says the soul-philosophers find "various characters ready-made in the mental life, and these they clap into the Soul"
  [[88]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-james-soul-verbal-explanation).
- **A vain word, or thinking matter.** La Mettrie: "The soul is therefore only a vain term for which we have no clear
  idea" [[26]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-lamettrie-soul-vain-term) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhPYlmkkDPjnLJSMdwn. Locke reportedly allows
  that subtle matter given sense and motion "might, with propriety of Speech, be called Spirit" ◐
  [[89]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-locke-thinking-matter-spirit). Al-Ghazālī reports the view that the soul depends on the body's composition
  [[90]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-tahafut-death-as-annihilation-view).

---

## Where the traditions disagree

- **Body or not.** Body (Stoics, Epicurus, Tertullian, Faustus); no body (Nemesius, Augustine, Avicenna, Proclus);
  a body of another order (More, the vehicle theorists, Kardec). Three answers, not two.
- **What number does.** For Xenocrates number *is* the soul. For Mamertus' Philolaus it is the soul's way into the
  body. For Mamertus himself it is the mark of bodies, which the soul lacks. For Psellos it is the soul's
  essential division.
- **Stuff versus process.** Qi gathers and disperses; the aggregates rise and pass. Both refuse a persisting thing,
  for opposite reasons: qi is in everything, the self in none of the aggregates.
- **Form.** Aquinas' form is a substance that can exist apart from the body; Fan Zhen's sharpness cannot.

## Critiques

- **Etymology is not meaning.** The breath-words left breath behind in different directions: nefesh counts persons,
  nafs is the source of evil, ātman is Brahman [[30]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-etymology-is-not-meaning).
- **The number-soul is atomism in disguise** [[42]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-grk-number-soul-collapses-into-atoms). It is also backdated: the oldest
  witness, Aristotle, names no Pythagorean [[91]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-grk-self-moving-number-backdated-to-pythagoras).
- **Immateriality is not demonstrated.** Al-Ghazālī, as Marmura summarises him, says Avicenna's proofs are not
  demonstrative [[92]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#isl-crit-ghazali-immateriality-not-demonstrated). Avicenna's answer to the temperament objection
  asserts more than it shows [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#isl-crit-flying-man-temperament). Kant: even a simple soul could fade by degrees
  [[93]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-mod-kant-remissio-against-simplicity-proofs).
- **The blade can be dull.** Xiao Chen answers Fan Zhen that sharpness comes from whetting [[94]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#chn-crit-xiaochen-dull-blade).
- **"Spirit" merges three words.** SL's English uses "spirit" for the Stoic body-pneuma, the vehicle and the daimon
  [[95]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#neo-crit-spirit-merges-three-words). In CH X SL inverts which garment wraps which [[96]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-hermetica-ch10-vestures-misrendered).
  It renders Synesius' "becomes earthy" as "grows proud" [[97]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-synesius-vehicle-earthy-misrendered).

## Open questions / what the canon reads would settle

- What Xenocrates meant by "self-moving number": the fragments are not held.
  Nemesius ch. 2 and Philoponus on De anima I are held and unread.
- Whether Mamertus' Philolaus is early Pythagorean. Unverified: modern editors class the fragment as spurious or
  doubtful ([unverified], ○).
- Proclus' full psychogony, In Tim. II, would place Psellos' seven terms.
- Zhang Zai's *Zhengmeng* is not on SL; it is known only through quotations.

title: 2. Where does the soul sit?
md:
**The question.** If the soul is in the body, is it somewhere in particular: the heart, the brain, the blood, a
gland, the organs? Or is it whole in every part, or in no place at all? The answer depends on page 01. A soul made
of stuff has a location. A soul with no size can only be "present" to the body.

**How to read it.** Claims are ✓ verified unless marked ◐ or ○. Quotes are SL's English, a model translation,
unless the book is English or the original is given. Tag: `q:where`.

**The short answer.**
- **The heart**: Chrysippus, Egypt, the Chinese 心藏神 [[1]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-chrysippus-hegemonikon-in-heart) [[2]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-bod-ch30-my-heart-my-mother) [[3]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-five-viscera-store-shen-hun-po).
- **The brain and its ventricles**: the Pythagorean notes, Nemesius, Avicenna [[4]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoreans-nous-phrenes-thymos-heart-brain) [[5]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-nemesius-ventricles-of-the-brain) [[6]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-internal-senses-ventricles).
- **The blood**: Critias, and Horapollo's hawk [[7]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-critias-soul-is-blood) [[8]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-horapollo-hawk-baieth).
- **The pineal gland**: Descartes, as the place it *acts*, not where it *is* [[9]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-gland-exercises-functions) [[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-em-pineal-is-not-where-the-soul-is).
- **Several organs at once**: 心藏神 肺藏魄 肝藏魂 [[3]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-five-viscera-store-shen-hun-po) [[11]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-guanyinzi-hun-eyes-po-liver).
- **Whole in every part**: Mamertus, Aquinas, Descartes [[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-mamertus-soul-whole-in-the-body-as-god-in-the-world) [[13]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-aquinas-whole-soul-in-each-part) [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-soul-joined-whole-body).
- **Nowhere, or partly outside**: Plotinus, Augustine, the antaryāmin, and the Buddhist denial of an inner seer [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-plotinus-undescended-soul) [[16]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-brihad-antaryamin-inner-controller) [[17]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-milinda-vedagu-living-principle).

---

## A. The heart

**The Stoic argument from the voice.** Chrysippus puts the ruling part (ἡγεμονικόν) in the heart because speech and
thought have one source:

> "These things occur manifestly around the heart, being sent forth from the heart through the throat and the voice"
> [[1]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-chrysippus-hegemonikon-in-heart) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bh4JoOM2z0Yjwt90upK
> (ταῦτα δὲ ἐκφανῶς περὶ τὴν καρδίαν γίγνεται)

The Pythagorean notes split the soul between the two organs. Thymos is in the heart, nous and phrenes in the brain
[[4]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoreans-nous-phrenes-thymos-heart-brain). A scholion to Epicurus puts the rational part in the chest
[[18]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-epicurus-soul-scattered-incorporeal-foolish).

**The Egyptian heart.** In Budge's English the heart (ab, ib) "was believed to be the source both of life and of
good and evil in man" [[19]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1898-heart-ab-life-good-evil) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgxPfJ7J9DwYCJgeqB1. It is
a witness who could testify against its owner:

> "O my heart, my mother ; O my heart, my mother ! O my heart of my existence upon earth. May naught stand up to
> oppose me in judgment in the presence of the lords of the trial" [[2]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-bod-ch30-my-heart-my-mother)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgxPfJ7J9DwYCJgeqE7

At the judgment "the heart was only required to balance the fea- ther and not to outweigh it"
[[20]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-bod-weighing-heart-feather). Horapollo's Greek reading of the hieroglyph ties soul and heart in one word: "Bai
enim anima est, eth cor" [[8]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-horapollo-hawk-baieth) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhbmmpYzEAVGMMQk5s0. In his Greek the hawk,
in sympathy with the soul, drinks blood, ᾧ καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ τρέφεται ("by which the soul too is nourished", our English).

**The Islamic heart.** Ibn Ṭufayl separates three senses of *qalb*:

> "I do not mean by the "heart" the physical heart, nor the spirit in its cavity, but I mean the form of that spirit
> overflowing with its powers upon the human body." [[21]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ibntufayl-three-senses-of-heart)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BijWMYoRxgM52PNK0TE (ولست اعني بالقلب جسم القلب ولا الروح الذي في تجويفه)

Al-Ghazālī's spirit "which we call heart" has no size at all [[22]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-heart-spirit-no-quantity). So "heart"
names an organ, a vapour in it, and something with no place, all in one word.

## B. The brain and its ventricles

Nemesius maps the inner faculties onto the brain's cavities. The front ventricles are the roots of the senses, the
middle one is for thinking, and the back one for memory:

> "The organ of this memory faculty is the posterior ventricle of the brain , which they call the cerebellum  or
> paracranis, and the psychic breath  found within it." [[5]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-nemesius-ventricles-of-the-brain)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUueghyIdnCELWcZRC (καὶ τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ ψυχικὸν πνεῦμα)

Avicenna's Latin puts the cogitative power "in the middle cavity of the brain where the worm is" (*in media
concavitate cerebri ubi est vermis*) [[6]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-internal-senses-ventricles) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPvFJDMtTfiFzRGYDJ.
Synesius has nature build the whole head around the imaginative pneuma, which rules from there as from an acropolis
[[23]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-synesius-pneuma-first-body). Swedenborg: "The cortical brain holds the inmost and the highest"
[[24]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-swedenborg-cortex-highest). A Daoist bedtime rite sends the second hun to guard the Niwan (泥丸), the head's
elixir field [[25]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zunsheng-refine-three-hun-guard-seven-po).

What sits in the ventricles is a faculty carried by a pneuma, not the soul. That is why the same authors can say
the soul itself has no place (section F).

## C. The blood

Aristotle reports that Critias took perception as the soul's mark and traced perception to the blood: "Another group
(Critias, for example) did hold it to be blood" [[7]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-critias-soul-is-blood) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bkp1LfgqJZJGMHrwQhT.
Horapollo says the hawk drinks blood, by which the soul is nourished
[[8]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-horapollo-hawk-baieth). Al-Hujwīrī lists blood among the meanings some give to nafs, and rejects them all
[[26]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-hujwiri-nafs-source-of-evil). Saint-Martin's animal soul "n'est autre chose que l'âme de sang"
[[27]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-render-ame-charnelle-saint-martin) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bg4FP6y7FDXJvgj5UD1. Avicenna's floating man
affirms his self without "heart, nor blood", which denies both seats at once [[28]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-flying-man-not-heart-blood).

## D. The pineal gland

Descartes is remembered for this answer, and the KB's reading of his text is that he did not give it. The heading
of Passions I.31 says:

> "That there is a gland in the brain, in which the soul exercises its functions more particularly than in the other
> parts." [[9]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-gland-exercises-functions) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhI8fARDfzZd3a9A69W
> (in qua anima suas functiones specialius quam in aliis partibus exerceat)

His reason is that the gland is single: "the other parts of our brain are all of them double"
[[29]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-gland-only-single-organ) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bem7jVjfaKUv32QqN8W. But the article before says
the soul "is truly joined to the whole body" [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-soul-joined-whole-body), and that it has "no relation to
extension, or dimensions" [[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-em-pineal-is-not-where-the-soul-is). The gland is where soul and body interact.

## E. Several organs: the Chinese viscera

In the medical scheme each organ stores its own spirit:

> "心藏神肺藏魄肝藏魂脾藏意腎藏志是為五臟所 藏" (our paraphrase: the heart stores shen, the lungs po, the liver hun,
> the spleen yi, the kidneys zhi) [[3]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-five-viscera-store-shen-hun-po) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl0VVfQE8eJmo0QhjF7

De Groot, as the claim reports, calls the liver the chief store of the hwun. The Guan Yinzi moves the seats by day
and night: by day the hun lodges in the eyes and one sees, by night the po lodges in the liver and one dreams
[[11]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-guanyinzi-hun-eyes-po-liver). The three hun can leave the body on fixed evenings each month and must be held
back by a method [[30]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-pujifang-three-hun-names-leave-body). The hun is the essence of the body (魂者身之精也)
[[31]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zhaohun-hun-essence-of-body). A seat here is a lodging. It can be left, and it can be called back to
(page 06).

## F. Whole in every part

Faustus of Riez put a dilemma: a soul is either somewhere, and so a body, or nowhere. Mamertus answers with God:

> "just as God is everywhere whole in the universe, so this [the soul] is found everywhere whole in the body."
> [[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-mamertus-soul-whole-in-the-body-as-god-in-the-world) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUuUqHu9PeRkqljwWX
> (sicut deus ubique totus in … uniuersitate, ita haec ubique tota inuenitur in corpore)

Aquinas makes it precise: "the whole soul is in each part of the body, it possesses the totality of perfection and
essence, though not according to all its power in every part of the body" [[13]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-aquinas-whole-soul-in-each-part)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPwp560jwjz5r3SiGc. Descartes: "it cannot properly be said to be in any one part of it,
to the exclusion of the others" [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-soul-joined-whole-body) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhI8fARDfzZd3a9A69V.
In the *Meditations*:

> "Nature teaches me that I am not merely present in my body as a sailor is present in a ship . Instead, I am very
> closely joined to it and, as it were, intermingled with it" [[32]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-not-sailor-in-ship)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bf1JGWG33XE1qAuO7cs (vt nauta adest nauigio)

The *Discours* says the same against the pilot [[33]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-descartes-soul-expressly-created-not-pilot).

Two bodily versions of "everywhere" stand beside these. For Epicurus the soul's particles are "dispersed all over
the frame" [[34]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-epicurus-soul-fine-particles-wind-heat). For Tertullian the soul has the shape of the very body
it fills [[35]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-tertullian-soul-shape-of-its-body). The Jain jīva is "सदेहपरिमाणो", equal in extent to its own body
[[36]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-jain-jiva-definition) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgRs5Lf5wXdyR5sWCa1.

## G. Nowhere, or not all here

- **No place because no size.** Augustine's soul is "not long, nor wide" [[37]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-augustine-quantity-of-soul-not-long-or-wide).
  Al-Kindī's "nor is it circumscribed" [[38]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-kindi-soul-not-body-not-circumscribed).
- **No place because perception is one.** Plotinus: "one thing does not perceive the nose, and another the eyes,
  but the same thing perceives at once all the parts of the face" [[39]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-plotinus-iv7-unity-of-perception)
  https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bi8TYwtni7t7sPx5onw. A pain relayed to a ruling part would need a regress.
- **Not all of it came down.** "the whole of our soul also does not enter into body, but something belonging to it
  always abides in the intelligible" [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-plotinus-undescended-soul) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bi8TVXMpLHijB36KakL
  (page 03).
- **Inside everything, as its controller.** The ātman dwells "in the earth, yet is other than the earth, whom the
  earth does not know" [[16]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-brihad-antaryamin-inner-controller) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTWpKOzEuBoNwN1Wjx.
- **No inner seer at all.** King Milinda asks for a soul that looks out through the eye as from a palace window.
  Nāgasena: "And so herein there is no such thing as soul (Vedagu)" [[17]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-milinda-vedagu-living-principle)
  https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgRlBroc5VJM6ITuBP9.
- **The brain as a switchboard.** Bergson: the brain's role "se borne à transmettre et à diviser du mouvement"
  [[40]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-bergson-brain-transmits-movement), and the body enters only the last plane of consciousness
  [[41]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-bergson-body-intervenes-last-plane). Carus, by contrast, assumes a bodily condition for every mental
  stirring, too fine to weigh [[42]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-carus-unconscious-processes-bodily-condition).

## H. After death: tomb, tablet, garden

The question of a seat outlives the body, and page 06 takes it up. In brief: the Egyptians call tombs eternal
homes (ἀϊδίους οἴκους) [[43]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-diodorus-eternal-homes). The ka can dwell in a statue [[44]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1898-ka-double-eidolon).
Chapter 89 prays "that my soul may come unto me from wheresoever it may be" [[45]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-bod-ch89-soul-united-to-body).
In China "冢以藏形廟以安神": the tomb stores the form, the temple settles the spirit
[[46]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-tianzhongji-burying-shen-banned). A priest calls the soul into the tablet [[47]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-degroot-soul-into-tablet),
and a garment calls the hun back to the po [[48]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-fayuan-zhulin-call-hun-not-po). In Duhem's Zohar the nefesh
"remains in the tomb as long as there are bones" [[49]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-duhem-zohar-nefesh-stays-in-tomb) while the ruach goes to
the earthly Garden [[50]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-myer-zohar-ruach-garden-neshamah-returns). The Hebrew dead are shades in Sheol
[[51]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-dewette-rephaim-joyless-shades) [[52]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-tylor-sheol-isaiah14-mighty-dead).

---

## Where the traditions disagree

- **Heart or brain.** This is a dispute about the *ruling* part. Chrysippus argues from the voice, the Pythagorean
  notes split the soul between the organs, and the ventricle tradition hands the brain the faculties, not the soul.
- **Seat or presence.** A soul of stuff has a seat (Epicurus, Tertullian, the Chinese viscera). A soul without size
  is present whole to the whole (Mamertus, Aquinas, Descartes) and only acts more in one place.
- **One seat or many.** The Chinese scheme gives each spirit its own organ. The Greek and Latin schemes give one
  soul several organs for its powers. That is the difference between page 03's "many souls" and "many parts".

## Critiques

- **Descartes did not put the soul in the pineal gland** [[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-em-pineal-is-not-where-the-soul-is). SL's English
  "it is the soul that senses, and not the body" keeps his *âme*, but the rendering of âme and esprit shifts across
  his pages [[53]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-render-ame-senses-descartes-dioptrique) [[54]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-vernacular-soul-spirit-mind).
- **Greek witnesses relocate the Egyptian dead.** Diodorus puts them in Hades, Herodotus gives them a transmigration
  no Egyptian text teaches [[55]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#egy-crit-greek-readers-platonize-egypt).
- **Avicenna's floating man** removes heart and blood from self-awareness, but his answer to the temperament
  objection asserts rather than shows [[56]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#isl-crit-flying-man-temperament).

## Open questions / what the canon reads would settle

- Galen's *De placitis Hippocratis et Platonis* holds Chrysippus' full heart argument and Posidonius' reply; held,
  unread.
- Al-Ghazālī's *ʿAjāʾib al-qalb* would settle what "heart" means in his own Arabic.
- Swedenborg's *Oeconomia regni animalis* and *De cerebro* are not found on SL;
  the French *Passions* would check the Latin "specialius".
- The *Yunji qiqian* on the three hun and their lunar days is not on SL.

title: 3. How many parts, or how many souls?
md:
**The question.** Does a person have one soul with several powers, one soul in several parts, or several souls?
The answers range from one (Aquinas) to three, five, seven, eight and nine, and down to zero owners of many parts
(the Buddhist aggregates). The count often belongs to the observer, not the tradition. Page 09 surveys the
traditions that count *several souls*; this page sets them beside the parts and powers of one soul.

**How to read it.** Claims are ✓ verified unless marked ◐ or ○. Quotes are SL's English, a model translation,
unless the book is English or the original is given. Tag: `q:parts`.

**The short answer.**
- **One soul, many powers**: Aristotle (aliveness-kb), Avicenna, Aquinas, al-Kindī [[5]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-soul-is-one-powers-flow) [[6]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-aquinas-one-substantial-form).
- **One soul, three parts**: Plato's reason, spirit and appetite; the charioteer and two horses [[7]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plato-republic-thymoeides-third-part) [[8]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plato-phaedrus-charioteer).
- **One soul, eight parts**: the Stoics [[9]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-stoics-eight-parts-of-soul).
- **Two souls in one man**: Willis, Saint-Martin, the two nafs [[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-willis-two-souls) [[11]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-render-ame-charnelle-saint-martin) [[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-two-senses-of-nafs).
- **Three to five Hebrew names**: nefesh, ruach, neshamah (and chayah, yechidah) [[13]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-myer-zohar-ruach-garden-neshamah-returns).
- **Eight or nine Egyptian parts**: ka, ba, akh and the rest [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1913-whole-man).
- **Hun and po, or three hun and seven po** [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zichan-po-first-then-hun) [[16]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-daoist-three-hun-seven-po-emotions).
- **Seven principles**: Blavatsky [[17]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-blavatsky-seven-principles-table).
- **A part that never came down**: Plotinus, against Proclus [[18]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-plotinus-undescended-soul) [[19]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-211-descends-whole).
- **Five aggregates and no owner**: the Buddha, Nāgasena [[20]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-vinaya-anattalakkhana) [[21]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-milinda-chariot-designation).

---

## A. One soul with many powers

Aristotle's nested powers, nutritive in sensitive in rational, belong to aliveness-kb
([[1]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-deanima-nutritive-soul-first-and-most-common), [[2]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-deanima-soul-first-entelechy-organic-body)).
His heirs insist the powers do not make several souls. Avicenna:

> "Later, however, it will be declared to you that the soul is one, from which these powers flow into the limbs"
> [[5]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-soul-is-one-powers-flow) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPvFJDMtTfiFzRGYDE (*anima una*)

Al-Kindī says the soul is one thing and the sensing power is the soul itself [[22]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-kindi-soul-not-body-not-circumscribed).
Aquinas is the strictest:

> "there is no other substantial form in man except the intellective soul alone, and it itself contains all inferior
> forms by its power" [[6]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-aquinas-one-substantial-form) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPwp560jwjz5r3SiGZ (unius rei est una tantum forma substantialis)

Descartes adds that "a half or a third part of the soul can in no way be conceived" [[23]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-no-half-soul).
Augustine finds a trinity in one mind, "in memory, and understanding, and will" [[24]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-augustine-trinity-memory-understanding-will).
The Academy's lectures made the powers numbers, mind the monad and knowledge the dyad [[25]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plato-lectures-mind-monad-dyad) (page 01 F).
The ventricle tradition gives the powers separate rooms in the brain [[26]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-nemesius-ventricles-of-the-brain) [[27]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-internal-senses-ventricles) (page 02).

## B. Plato's three, and the chariot

In *Republic* IV the city's three classes give the soul a third element besides reason and appetite:

> "may there not be in the individual soul a third element which is passion or spirit, and which is the auxiliary
> of reason when not corrupted by education?" [[7]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plato-republic-thymoeides-third-part)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BeqYUOswGqYzFfFK4B8 (θυμοειδές, λογιστικόν, ἐπιθυμητικόν)

The *Phaedrus* gives a likeness instead of an account: "We will liken the soul to the composite nature of a pair of
winged horses and a charioteer." Even the gods' souls are such teams [[8]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plato-phaedrus-charioteer)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTma6xEUveMD9g1WBG. The Pythagorean notes make a different three: nous, phrenes and
thymos, of which only the phrenes are human and immortal [[28]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoreans-nous-phrenes-thymos-heart-brain).

The Kaṭha Upaniṣad has a chariot too: "Know thou the soul (ātman, self) as riding in a chariot, The body as the
chariot." There buddhi is the driver, manas the reins, and the self is the passenger [[29]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-katha-chariot-soul)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTWpKOzEuBoNwN1Wnl. The Muṇḍaka splits the self into two birds on one tree, one eating
and one watching [[30]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-mundaka-two-birds).

## C. The Stoic eight

> "They count eight parts of the soul: the five senses, the generative power in us, our power of speech, and that of
> reasoning." [[9]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-stoics-eight-parts-of-soul) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhAwalpTYhD8XcOymwb (μέρη ψυχῆς ὀκτώ)

The eight are functions of one pneuma, which runs from a ruling part in the heart [[31]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-chrysippus-hegemonikon-in-heart).

## D. Two souls in one person

Thomas Willis gives man a corporeal soul shared with the brutes and a rational one, and asks "How both souls are
joined in a human." [[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-willis-two-souls) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bh9MpeDWI2wky57PpSO (Quomodo utræque animæ in
homine conjunguntur). Saint-Martin's âme charnelle "n'est autre chose que l'âme de sang", beside an "âme
intelligente et spirituelle" [[11]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-render-ame-charnelle-saint-martin). Swedenborg has "a superior mind and an
inferior mind (or mind properly so called)" [[32]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-swedenborg-superior-inferior-mind).

In Islam the split runs through one word. Al-Ghazālī, as Macdonald reports, uses nafs for the soul that commands to
evil and for "the very essence of man which knows God and all knowable things" [[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-two-senses-of-nafs).
Al-Hujwīrī's masters agree that nafs is "the source of evil and the basis of wickedness" [[33]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-hujwiri-nafs-source-of-evil).
A Persian treatise lists six levels, from ammāra to marḍiyya (اماره و لوامه و ملهمه و مطمئنه و راضیه و مرضیه)
[[34]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-nafs-six-levels-fez-persian). Al-Ghazālī's *Mishkāt* reads the Light Verse as five spirits, the sensory
spirit being the niche [[35]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-mishkat-five-spirits).

## E. Nefesh, ruach, neshamah, and the five names

Page 09 D has the five names, from Menasseh ben Israel ([[3]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-menasseh-five-names-of-soul)). In the
Zohar the three lower ones part at death. "The Rua'h ascends into the Garden which is on earth … The Neshamah, she
ascends at once to that same place she came out from" [[13]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-myer-zohar-ruach-garden-neshamah-returns)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhtuqyFGsWBkYY9K2Uv. The nefesh "remains in the tomb as long as there are bones."
[[36]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-duhem-zohar-nefesh-stays-in-tomb). Moses de León defines the neshamah as "the true intellect, hewn from the
source of life" (השכל האמיתי אשר ממקור החיים נחצב) [[37]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-disputatio-neshamah-true-intellect). A further soul can be
added: in *ibbur* "the soul of a Righteous man is poured into the soul of the living, like light proceeding from
light" [[38]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-disputatio-ibbur-righteous-soul-poured-in). Yet the Zohar also says the three are all one in one
([[4]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-zohar-nefesh-ruach-neshamah-all-one)). In Genesis, says Solovyov, nephesh chayah is the natural
life man shares with animals [[39]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-render-nefesh-chayah-solovyov).

## F. Ka, ba, akh: the Egyptian eight

Budge (1913) counts the person:

> "Thus, as we have seen, the whole man consisted of a natural body, a Spirit-body, a heart, a double, a Heart-soul, a
> shadow, a Spirit-soul, and a name. All these were, however, bound together inseparably" [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1913-whole-man)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgxPfzQIozZpXOIK0TP

The parts are named one by one: khat and sāḥu [[40]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1898-khat-sahu-spiritual-body), the ka as "double"
[[41]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1898-ka-double-eidolon), the ba [[42]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1913-ba-heart-soul), the khu or akh as "Spirit-soul"
[[43]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1913-khu-spirit-soul), the khaibit or shadow [[44]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1913-khaibit-skia-umbra). The ka is
undecided: "What the KA really was has not yet been decided" [[45]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1913-ka-genius-or-double). Tylor's list
from Birch has four, ba, akh, ka, khaba [[46]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-tylor-birch-ba-akh-ka-khaba). A 1907 Theosophical manual has
seven, without endorsing their accuracy [[47]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-tingley-1907-seven-egyptian-souls).

## G. Hun and po, three and seven

Zichan's speech of 535 BCE is the oldest account: "人生始化曰魄、既生魄陽曰魂", at birth the first transformation is
po, and its yang is hun [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zichan-po-first-then-hun) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOlWFAjYWGMUOylWYg. The
*Lingshu* defines them by what they move with: hun goes with shen, po with jing [[48]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-lingshu-benshen-hun-po-defined).
Zhu Xi assigns them work: "凡能記憶皆魄之所藏受也至於 運用發出來是魂" (our paraphrase: memory is what po stores;
what issues into use is hun) [[49]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zhuxi-po-stores-hun-issues) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl0Z6vbM1oIUBaHWrlp. The
*Xingli daquan* gives knowing to hun and the frame to po [[50]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-xingli-knowing-hun-body-po).

The Daoist count is three hun and seven po. One commentary makes the seven po the seven emotions:

> "所謂三 魂者即此元神真而七魄者喜怒哀懼愛惡欲也 全魂即為仙全魄即為鬼魂與魄兩立則為人" (our paraphrase: the three hun are
> the Original Spirit, the seven po are joy, anger, sorrow, fear, love, hate and desire; all hun makes an immortal,
> all po a ghost, both together a human) [[16]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-daoist-three-hun-seven-po-emotions) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BkB9R72sTMLMF7lzJ92

The three hun have names and leave the body on fixed nights [[51]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-pujifang-three-hun-names-leave-body), and a rite
sets them to guard [[52]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zunsheng-refine-three-hun-guard-seven-po). De Groot says the three-and-seven doctrine is
Daoist and not based on the ancients [[53]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-degroot-three-seven-not-ancient). He himself calls hun
and po "the soul in its two component parts" [[54]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-degroot-hwun-poh-one-soul). Legge renders po "the animal soul"
and hun "the spirit" [[55]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-legge-hunpo-soul-and-spirit).

## H. Seven principles

Blavatsky's *Key to Theosophy* has a lower four (body, prāṇa, the astral double, kāma-rūpa) and an upper three
(manas, buddhi, ātma): "(c) Linga Sharira. (c) Astral body. (c) The Double, the phantom body."
[[17]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-blavatsky-seven-principles-table). Leadbeater has man leave "no less than three corpses" [[56]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-leadbeater-three-corpses).
Psellos' sevenfold soul is a different seven, the seven terms of *Timaeus* 35 [[57]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-psellos-soul-sevenfold).

## I. The undescended part

Plotinus breaks with the school:

> "the whole of our soul also does not enter into body, but something belonging to it always abides in the
> intelligible, and something different from this in the sensible world" [[18]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-plotinus-undescended-soul)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bi8TVXMpLHijB36KakL

Proclus, after Iamblichus, denies it: "Every particular soul, descending into generation, descends as a whole."
[[19]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-211-descends-whole) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUvVF7tfKHgyDbC4OR. A part that always thought
unchanged would be intellect, not soul [[58]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#neo-crit-whole-descent-against-undescended).

## J. Five aggregates and no owner

The Buddha takes the five khandhas one by one:

> "The body (Rûpa), O Bhikkhus, is not the self." [[20]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-vinaya-anattalakkhana) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhPXIeb5uGyl6M9xHQ8

The same is said of sensation, perception, the saṃkhāras and consciousness. Nāgasena finds no chariot among the
parts, all the parts together, or outside them: "Chariot is a mere empty sound." [[21]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-milinda-chariot-designation)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgRlBroc5VJM6ITuBOQ. The Tengyur records the objection: if the aggregates are not the self,
who experiences the fruit of deeds? (རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པ་བདག་མ་ཡིན་ན།) [[59]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-tengyur-who-experiences-karma). This is a count of
many parts with no soul, the opposite of Aquinas' one soul with no parts.

## K. Modern divisions

Jung separates *Psyche*, all psychic processes, from *Seele*, "einen bestimmten, abgegrenzten Funktionskomplex"
[[60]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-jung-seele-vs-psyche), and gives a man a feminine soul [[61]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-jung-anima-contrasexual-soul). Myers speaks of
a subliminal Self, without "two correlative and parallel selves" [[62]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-myers-subliminal-self). James's
consciousness "is nothing jointed; it flows" [[63]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-james-stream-of-thought).

---

## Where the traditions disagree

- **Parts or souls.** Plato's parts can fight but cannot leave. Hun and po, ruach and neshamah, ka and ba go to
  different places at death (page 06). That is the test page 09 uses.
- **Counts or names.** The midrash's five are names of one soul; the Zohar's are levels with separate fates. Budge's
  eight are one person "bound together inseparably".
- **One owner, or none.** Aquinas: one form, all powers. The Buddha: all the parts, no owner. Plotinus: one soul, part
  of it never here.

## Critiques

- **"The soul" presumes one per person**, but nearly every tradition on SL counts several; Tylor lists them and files
  them as speculation from "the savage condition of our race" [[64]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-one-soul-per-person) [[65]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-tylor-plural-souls-savage-condition).
- **Hun and po are not two halves of one soul.** They are configurations of qi that part in opposite directions
  [[66]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#chn-crit-soul-flattens-hun-po).
- **Budge's English for the Egyptian parts is unstable** from book to book [[67]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#egy-crit-soul-for-ba-unstable); the
  frame is developmental [[68]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#egy-crit-primitive-frame); SL adds its own gloss to "heart-soul" [[69]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-render-ba-gloss-inserted-greenfield).
- **The septenary is back-projected** onto India, Plato, Paul and Egypt [[70]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-mod-theosophy-septenary-back-projection).
- **The chariot is three doctrines** (Plato, Kaṭha, Milinda) [[71]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-ind-chariot-is-not-phaedrus).
- **SL's English shifts.** Thymos is "spirit" and "life" on one page [[72]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-homer-thymos-rendered-spirit-and-life). A
  Republic manuscript gets an invented "medicine" [[73]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-republic-ms-medicine-mistranslation).

## Open questions / what the canon reads would settle

- Maimonides' five faculties (*Shemonah Peraqim* 1) has no clean print.
- Iamblichus' *De anima* in Stobaeus would give the whole-descent argument at source.
- Vasubandhu's refutation of the person, *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* 9.
- The Shangqing texts on three hun and seven po are not on SL.
- Unverified: Walker's Oglala four souls ([unverified], ○; see page 09 E).

title: 4. Who has a soul?
md:
**The question.** Do plants have souls? Animals? The world, the stars, the gods? Is there anything without one? The
answer follows from page 01. Where soul is life, every living thing has one. Where soul is reason, only humans and
higher beings do. Where soul is qi, nothing lacks it. This page also asks briefly about artifacts; page 08 asks it
properly.

**How to read it.** Claims are ✓ verified unless marked ◐ or ○. Quotes are SL's English, a model translation,
unless the book is English or the original is given. Tag: `q:who-has`.

**The short answer.**
- **Plants**: yes for Aristotle (aliveness-kb), the Vedas, the Jains and Fechner; living but soulless for the
  Pythagorean notes [[9]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-jain-tattvartha-one-sensed-jivas) [[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-chandogya-trees-conscious-gloss) [[11]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoreans-soul-distinct-from-life).
- **Animals**: yes, but a soul that cannot see itself; or one that reasons better than ours
  [[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-mamertus-beasts-cannot-see-themselves) [[13]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-rorarius-brutes-reason-better).
- **The world**: the Stoic soul of the whole, Plato's living cosmos (aliveness-kb), More's Spirit of Nature
  [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-stoics-soul-connate-pneuma-survives-until-conflagration) [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-more-phantasm-soul-fabric-spirit-of-nature).
- **Stars, gods and the king**: the ba of Pepi is a star [[16]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-pyramid-pepi-soul-star) [[17]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1911-vocab-ba-of-gods).
- **Everything**: qi in all things; the ātman in earth and wind [[18]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zhuxi-guishen-only-qi) [[19]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-brihad-antaryamin-inner-controller).
- **Only some humans fully**: al-Fārābī's virtuous, the Kabbalists' Israel [[20]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-farabi-which-souls-survive) [[21]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-disputatio-zohar-kuzari-israel-holy-souls).
- **Artifacts**: only by a gift from outside (page 08) [[22]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-aristotle-axe-would-have-soul) [[23]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-mach-ensouled-artifacts-are-not-precedents).

---

## A. Plants: soul, life, or neither

Aristotle's answer, that plants have the nutritive soul, is in aliveness-kb ([[1]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-deanima-nutritive-soul-first-and-most-common)).
The Pythagorean notes separate life from soul:

> "All things live which partake of heat—this is why plants are living things—but all do not have a soul."
> [[11]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoreans-soul-distinct-from-life) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhAwalpTYhD8XcOymxx (ζωή vs ψυχή)

Yet Pythagoras is also said to remember "how it traveled into various plants and animals" [[24]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoras-euphorbus-soul-wanderings)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhAwalpTYhD8XcOymxc. So a plant can at least house a soul.

In India the question was disputed by school. Müller's note to the Chāndogya: "The commentator remarks that
according to the Veda, trees are conscious, while Buddhists and followers of Kanâda hold them to be unconscious."
[[10]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-chandogya-trees-conscious-gloss) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgRlE6p1aSOPvppKu8N. The Jains go furthest. Earth,
water, fire, air and plants are all one-sensed jīvas:

> "पृथिव्यप्तेजोवायुवनस्पतयः स्थावराः" (earth, water, fire, air and plants are the immobile beings)
> [[9]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-jain-tattvartha-one-sensed-jivas) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgRs6Rd32OkfEIJ3pti (स्थावर, sthāvara)

Mamertus grades creation: essence in stones, seminal life in plants, sensual life in beasts, rational life in man
[[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-mamertus-beasts-cannot-see-themselves). Fechner asks why an artificial flower never smiles at us like a
living one: "weil wir nur in dieser nicht in jener eine wirklich lachende Seele ahnen" [[25]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-fechner-nanna-artificial-flower)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOcWgAfDFur4esBIQt. His argument for plant souls is in aliveness-kb
([[2]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/romantic-naturphilosophie#rom-fechner-1848-plants-souls-nature-feels-herself)). For Proclus even the heliotrope prays
([[3]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lat-proclus-plants-pray)).

## B. Animals: a soul that cannot see itself

Almost every tradition here gives animals a soul. The question is what kind.

**Lacking self-knowledge.** Mamertus:

> "not possessing the eye of reasoning, they cannot see—I will not say something above themselves—but they cannot
> see themselves" [[12]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-mamertus-beasts-cannot-see-themselves) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUuUqHu9PeRkqljwVB

Willis makes the brute soul corporeal and gives man a second, rational one [[26]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-willis-two-souls). The rational
soul's object is "all being" [[27]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-willis-human-mind-object-all-being). Pico's brutes "bring with them from "their
mother’s womb" (as Lucilius says) all that they will ever possess", while man can become anything
[[28]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-pico-brutes-bring-all-from-womb).

**Sharing one breath.** Ecclesiastes: "all have one spirit; and man has no advantage over the beast" (וְרוּחַ אֶחָד
לַכֹּל) [[29]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-eccl3-one-ruach-man-and-beast) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiFm0ilKGU0npyYuAqT. Blavatsky notes that
nephesh "was indifferently applied to immortal man and to mortal beast" [[30]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-render-nefesh-blavatsky-life-and-living-soul).

**Reasoning better.** Rorario's title says it: "QVOD ANIMALIA BRVTA Saepe ratione utantur meliùs Homine."
[[13]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-rorarius-brutes-reason-better) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BlATqFnQSC4Rfb9okXz. Bayle's article on him is
answered in the *Monadology* [[31]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-bayle-rorarius-article-monadology). Cudworth states the price of giving animals
substantial souls: they would survive death [[32]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-cudworth-brute-souls-immortal-objection).

**Holding a human soul.** Xenophanes mocks Pythagoras: "Stop, do not beat it, for it is the soul of a dear friend"
[[33]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-pythagoras-dog-soul-of-a-friend). Herodotus reports an Egyptian circuit of the soul through all creatures in
3,000 years [[34]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-herodotus-ii123-transmigration). Kircher's Kabbalists send sinners' souls into animals
[[35]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-kircher-levita-each-soul-three-bodies). The Hermetic *Key* has souls climb from creeping things to humans
[[36]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-hermetica-ch10-ladder-of-souls), but forbids the fall back: "Nor is it lawful for a human soul to fall into
the body of an irrational animal." [[37]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-hermetica-ch10-no-animal-body). Kardec agrees [[38]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-kardec-soul-is-incarnate-spirit).
In Homer, Circe's swine keep their minds: "yet their minds remained unchanged" [[39]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-homer-circe-noos-stays-in-swine).

## C. The world soul

Plato's cosmos as a living creature with soul and intelligence ([[4]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-timaeus-cosmos-zoon-empsychon-ennoun))
and Proclus' life-giving world soul ([[5]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-proclus-world-soul-zoogonia)) are in aliveness-kb; the
magical world soul is in magic-kb ([[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/arabic#ara-picatrix-certainty-world-soul)). Here the world soul matters as the
whole of which ours are parts. The Stoics make our souls parts of the soul of the whole, which alone is
imperishable [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-stoics-soul-connate-pneuma-survives-until-conflagration). Proclus' world soul makes the whole and
divides it "according to the essential dyad" [[40]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/neoplatonic-hermetic#neo-proclus-timaeus-soul-divides-by-dyad).

Henry More's Spirit of Nature organises matter without perception: "what Phantasme is to our Soul, that Fabrick is
to the Spirit of Nature" [[15]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/early-modern#em-more-phantasm-soul-fabric-spirit-of-nature) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BejWIDHvgIoRz3OeuKs.
William James finds an anima mundi thinking in all of us more promising, metaphysically, than many individual souls.
As a psychologist he still holds that "the passing Thought itself is the only verifiable thinker"
[[41]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/modern#mod-james-passing-thought-only-thinker). Spinoza's individuals are all "animata", in different degrees
([[7]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-spinoza-omnia-animata)).

## D. Stars, gods and the king's ba

The Pyramid Texts make the dead king's ba a star:

> "Behold Pepi this, thy soul is the Souls of Ánu; behold thy soul is the Souls of Nekhen; behold thy soul is the
> Souls of Pe; behold thy soul is a star living, behold, among its brethren" [[16]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-pyramid-pepi-soul-star)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgxPfzQIozZpXOIK0TM (bꜣw)

Gods have ba as men do: "ba the divine Soul, or soul of God. ba soul of Osiris; of Rā" [[17]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1911-vocab-ba-of-gods).
Alcmaeon's soul is immortal because it moves ceaselessly, like sun, moon and heaven [[42]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-alcmaeon-immortal-by-ceaseless-motion).
The gods' souls in the *Phaedrus* are charioteer teams with good horses [[43]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-plato-phaedrus-charioteer). Gilbert's
argument for star souls, in aliveness-kb, finds it pitiable that the worm should have a soul and the stars not
([[8]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-gilbert-soulless-stars-below-the-worm)). Faustus of Riez extends bodies upward instead: angels
and souls have thin bodies, and nothing is incorporeal except God (*nihil esse incorporeum, nisi solum deum*)
[[44]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/christian#chr-faustus-nothing-incorporeal-but-god).

## E. Everything: qi and the inner controller

In the Chinese texts the question has no edge. Zhu Xi says a person's qi is continuous with the qi of heaven and
earth: "人之氣 與天地之氣常相接無間斷" (our paraphrase: a person's qi and the qi of heaven and earth are always joined
without a break) [[18]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zhuxi-guishen-only-qi) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl0Z7VrdSkq9cVOvXbZ. Zhang Zai: the Great
Void cannot but have qi, and qi cannot but gather into the myriad things [[45]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-zhangzai-guishen-liangneng).
Day, spring and the rising tide are shen; night, autumn and the ebb are gui [[46]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/chinese-east-asian#chn-guishen-expansion-contraction-of-qi).
So the question is not who has a soul but how much qi is gathered, and how well.

In the Upaniṣads the ātman is in everything as its controller, "He who, dwelling in the earth, yet is other than
the earth" [[19]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-brihad-antaryamin-inner-controller), and "That art thou" (tat tvam asi) [[47]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-chandogya-tat-tvam-asi).
Sāṃkhya, by contrast, insists "there is a plurality of souls" [[48]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/indic#ind-sankhya-plurality-of-purushas).

## F. Not every human equally

- **By virtue.** Al-Fārābī: the souls of the ignorant cities "bleiben … unvollkommen" and perish with their matter,
  like beasts [[20]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-farabi-which-souls-survive) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BmiNukILiokqVv8wELe. Chrysippus lets only
  the souls of the wise last until the conflagration [[14]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/greek#grk-stoics-soul-connate-pneuma-survives-until-conflagration).
- **By people.** The Disputatio cites the Zohar: God gave Israel "holy souls from a holy place, above all other
  nations" [[21]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-disputatio-zohar-kuzari-israel-holy-souls), and the nations' souls do not come from the same place
  [[49]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/hebrew-kabbalah#heb-disputatio-souls-created-before-world-receptacle).
- **By rank.** Al-Ghazālī's highest spirit is the transcendental prophetic spirit of saints and prophets
  [[50]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-mishkat-five-spirits).

## G. Beasts that cannot see themselves, and machines

Mamertus' test returns for artifacts. A thing that stores and recalls images ranks with the beasts. On the KB's
machine table, a machine that only remembers fails his test in the same way [[51]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-row-mamertus). Aristotle excludes
the axe by the word "natural": "if this disappeared from it, it would have ceased to be an axe, except in name. As it
is, … it is just an axe" [[22]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-aristotle-axe-would-have-soul) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bkp1LfgqJZJGMHrwQhl. The
ensouled artifacts on SL get their soul from outside: the Asclepius' temple statues [[52]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-asclepius-man-fictor-deorum),
the ka in a statue [[53]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/egyptian-ane#egy-budge-1898-ka-double-eidolon), and Rava's man who "did not answer" [[54]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/soul-and-machine#mach-bahir-rava-man-did-not-answer).
Page 08 takes this up.

---

## Where the traditions disagree

- **Where the line falls.** Between living and non-living (Aristotle), between soul and life inside the living (the
  Pythagorean notes), between sense and reason (Mamertus, Willis), or nowhere (qi, the Jain elements).
- **Whether the line can be crossed.** Pythagoras, Herodotus' Egyptians and Kircher's Kabbalists let a human soul
  enter a beast. The Hermetic *Key* and Kardec forbid it. Aristotle mocks the idea: each soul needs its own body.
- **Up or down.** Faustus makes everything below God a body, souls and angels included. The Jains make everything
  down to earth and water a jīva.

## Critiques

- **Each soul needs its own body.** Aristotle: it is as absurd as carpentry embodying itself in flutes
  [[55]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-grk-each-soul-its-own-body).
- **Tylor's ladder from savage to cultured** makes animal and plant souls an extension of the human, and the
  extension a mistake [[56]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-tylor-doctrine-of-souls-savage-to-cultured) [[57]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-tylor-frame-shapes-world-glosses).
- **The Greek witnesses Platonize Egypt.** No Egyptian text teaches Herodotus' 3,000-year circuit
  [[58]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#egy-crit-greek-readers-platonize-egypt). Budge's "Holy Soul" and "soul of God" add Christian diction
  [[59]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-x-egypt-eternal-life-and-heaven).
- **Ensouled artifacts are not precedents**: the soul comes from outside the structure [[23]](/explore/histories/soul/claims/critique#crit-mach-ensouled-artifacts-are-not-precedents).

## Open questions / what the canon reads would settle

- The full Jain taxonomy of jīvas by senses and bodies, the *Gommaṭasāra Jīvakāṇḍa*.
- Rorario's dialogue and Bayle's "Rorarius" are held and unread;
  Pardies on the knowledge of beasts is not held.
